# Temple Scroll Column 47 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 47 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**47:1** And if she is married to a husband while her vows are upon her or the rash utterance of her lips by which she has bound herself —

**47:2** and her husband hears and is silent toward her on the day he hears — then her vows shall stand, and her binding obligations shall stand.

**47:3** But if on the day her husband hears he annuls them, then the LORD will forgive her.

**47:4** Every vow of a widow and of a divorced woman — everything by which she has bound herself shall stand against her.

**47:5** These are the statutes that the LORD commanded concerning vows between a man and his wife, and between a father and his daughter in her youth in her father's house.

**47:6** When a man or a woman makes a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite, to separate himself to the LORD —

**47:7** he shall abstain from wine and strong drink; he shall drink no vinegar of wine or vinegar of strong drink, and he shall not drink any juice of grapes, and he shall not eat grapes, fresh or dried.

**47:8** All the days of his separation he shall not eat anything that is produced by the grapevine, from the seeds to the skin.

**47:9** All the days of his vow of separation no razor shall come upon his head; until the days are fulfilled for which he separates himself to the LORD, he shall be holy; he shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow long.

**47:10** All the days of his separation to the LORD he shall not go near a dead body.

**47:11** He shall abstain from wine and strong drink; he shall drink no vinegar of wine or vinegar of strong drink, and he shall not drink any juice of grapes.

**47:12** For his father or for his mother, for his brother or for his sister — he shall not make himself unclean for them when they die, for the consecration of his God is upon his head.

**47:13** All the days of his separation he is holy to the LORD.

**47:14** And if anyone dies very suddenly beside him, and he defiles the head of his consecration, then he shall shave his head on the day of his cleansing — on the seventh day he shall shave it.

**47:15** And on the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest, to the entrance of the tent of meeting.

**47:16** And the priest shall offer one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering and make atonement for him, because he sinned on account of the dead body; and he shall sanctify his head on that day.

---

*EMET notes: Column 47 concludes the women's vow legislation (vv. 1-5) and transitions to the Nazirite vow (vv. 6-16), paralleling Numbers 6:1-12. The three Nazirite restrictions are preserved: abstinence from grape products (vv. 7-8, 11), no cutting of hair (v. 9), and no contact with the dead (vv. 10, 12). The emergency provision for accidental corpse contamination (vv. 14-16) follows Numbers 6:9-12.*
